## Current observation

The authoritative current work-state observation is:

- CYAX-0155 / Issue #155 is **CLOSED**, with state reason **COMPLETED**.
- Its Project Status is **Done**.

This is supported by `issue-155-current`. Under the governing workflow, Issues and Projects—not the specification or this frozen summary—track live work state (`sdd-contract-at-merge`).

## Historical instruction and unresolved condition

After PR #156 merged, the durable checkpoint said to **keep #155 open until the Research & Chats saved Project view/filter was configured**. It also expressly declined to claim that configuration was complete because the available connector could neither mutate nor directly verify Projects-v2 views (`issue-155-checkpoint`).

This was a remaining Project/workflow condition, distinct from the repository implementation:

- The approved specification requires Research & Chats to be a saved view rather than another authority layer. Its acceptance language says such a view “can be configured,” which does not unambiguously prove that a concrete view had to exist as part of the repository change (`spec-0155`).
- The PR classified actual saved-view configuration as a separate Projects-v2 operation and claimed no such mutation (`pr-156`).
- The human guide describes how the view works but records no concrete configured instance (`checkpoint-guide-at-merge`).

## Implementation evidence

The repository-side implementation is durably established:

- PR #156 was merged at `2026-09-11T00:01:20Z` with squash commit `f0013552cd69a93221464e9c8ccfd56339f39052` (`pr-156`).
- That commit updated the repository contract, SDD, human guide, and approved specification (`pr-156-merge-commit`).
- The checkpoint states that the repository-side privacy boundary was active on `vmm` (`issue-155-checkpoint`).

This supports implementation of the repository control-plane changes. It does **not** prove creation of the Project saved view.

## Later authority event

At `2026-09-11T01:09:18Z`, `vmmhep` closed Issue #155. That is the later authoritative work-state mutation and explains why the current state is Closed/Completed (`issue-155-closure-event`, `issue-155-current`).

However, the closure event contains no reason or explanatory text. It has no associated commit, was not performed through a GitHub App, and the merge message itself did not automatically close #155 (`issue-155-closure-event`, `pr-156-merge-commit`).

## Inference and unknowns

The defensible inference is that someone intentionally changed the governing Issue’s state after the keep-open checkpoint. It is **not** defensible to infer why.

The frozen evidence does not durably prove that:

- the Research & Chats saved view/filter was configured;
- the keep-open condition was expressly waived or superseded;
- the closer determined that the specification did not require a concrete view;
- the closure was accidental or erroneous; or
- the observed view configuration has remained unchanged.

The bounded artifact search found no later public evidence documenting configuration or explicitly superseding the condition (`closure-search`). That is an absence within the captured scope, not proof that configuration never occurred.

Therefore, I abstain from claiming either that the saved-view condition was satisfied or that it was validly superseded.

## Next valid verification or action

Directly inspect the current **CYAxiverse Research & Development** Project configuration using a Projects-v2-capable UI or API and verify whether a saved **Research & Chats** view/filter exists with the intended normal Status field and sanitized metadata.

- If it exists, record a durable, sanitized Issue checkpoint documenting that verification.
- If it does not exist, configure it or obtain an explicit authoritative waiver/supersession; then reconcile Issue #155’s Closed/Done state with the earlier keep-open instruction.

Until that direct verification occurs, the authoritative state remains **Closed/Completed and Done**, while satisfaction or supersession of the saved-view condition remains **unknown**.
